engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health engaged Treya Partners to identify and capture cost-savings across its purchased goods and services, and to establish stronger procurement processes and controls in order to increase EBITDA and enterprise value ahead of a future exit.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project targets 10 spend categories representing roughly $19 million in annual spend (≈$45 million total company spend, $18.9 million addressable). Work includes competitive events, incumbent negotiations, and GPO leverage, plus a review of procurement processes/controls. Employee Benefits is an optional later work-stream; other categories may be excluded if found non-addressable after deep dives.
constraints_challenges: Decentralized, multi-site purchasing split between Mid-Atlantic and Heartland business units
Limited strategic procurement resources and focus within Advantia
Incomplete line-item and usage data; must be collected from high-spend suppliers
Multiple AP/P-card systems with inconsistent vendor naming and minimal backend integration from acquisitions
Potential pushback from long-standing incumbent suppliers and the need to avoid disruption to clinical operations
Aggressive six-month timeline for most categories, with Benefits workstream deferred and capped at four months

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts Payable data for Oct-2020–Sep-2021 from two systems and YTD P-card data were available; contracts and detailed usage must be obtained directly from suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend spread across separate systems, supplier names not standardized; item-level data often missing, and some suppliers may never provide it despite repeated requests.
